title: sacrum, buttocks and hips

chart.description: The sacrum, buttocks and the sides of the hips unrolled round a horizontal section of the skin. u: arc length (cm) from the posterior median line, positive towards the patient's LEFT, round to the front of the hips. v: height (cm) above the level of the posterior superior iliac spines. d: depth below the skin along the inward normal (cm).

description: Over the sacrum the skin and a thin layer of fat and ligaments lie on bone, with the four posterior sacral foramina in two rows either side of the median sacral crest (the second level with the posterior superior iliac spines); a needle in a foramen passes towards the sacral nerve roots and the pelvis. Lateral to the sacrum the thick gluteal muscles cover the ilium and the hip; the sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis below piriformis and runs down midway between the greater trochanter and the ischial tuberosity, several centimetres deep.

review.notes: Depths below the skin of the lungs, organs, bones and great vessels are measured on one reference body (a 38-year-old man of about 90 kg) and scaled to each patient by height and BMI; the rest is schematic. Not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.

provenance.notes: Depth grid (2 cm): depths of the sacrum, ilium, femur, bowel and bladder measured by rays on the reference body; the sacral foramina (small zones), the fat/ligament split and the course of the sciatic nerve (anchored to the measured greater trochanter and ischial tuberosity) are schematic.
